rationale: M59 (#825). Every line below is read off import-multiline-825.scala. An import reference is a References edge whose target is the dotted module, and the analyzer appends a RENAMED selector to that module (`{mutable => mut}` imports `scala.collection.mutable`). The old line came from the import statement's start, so the edge claimed line 11 (`import scala.collection.{`) while the name it names — `mutable` — is written on line 12. Found on real code: the store check's single remaining inconsistent line on cats-effect was `cats.effect.kernel.testkit.TestInstances`, whose renamed segment is written nine lines after the statement opens. The forbid entry is the pre-fix behaviour.

forbidRelationships.note: pre-fix: the import statement's opening line; the segment `mutable` that names the target is written on 12
